---
title: "Glossary"
description: "What the numbers on Sparvi mean and how they're calculated."
---

## Pitching

**Stuff+**: Pitch quality graded only on physical traits (velocity, movement, spin, release point, extension, arm angle, and gaps from the pitcher's primary fastball). 100 is an average qualified MLB pitcher; 10 points is one standard deviation. Pitch-level grades are scaled within fastballs, breaking balls, and offspeed pitches. [How it's built](/baseball/stuff-plus/#method).

**RV+**: Actual run value per 100 pitches, on the same scale as Stuff+.

**IVB (induced vertical break)**: How far a pitch finishes above or below where a spinless pitch would, in inches. High-IVB fastballs "ride"; curveballs have negative IVB.

**HB (horizontal break)**: Sideways movement in inches, **positive toward the pitcher's arm side** for both righties and lefties, so shapes compare directly.

**FB velo**: Average velocity of the pitcher's primary fastball: the four-seamer or sinker thrown most over the season. "Velo Δ14" compares that same pitch over the final 14 days with its season average.

**CSW rate**: Called strikes plus whiffs, divided by pitches.

**Chase induced**: Share of pitches outside the zone that the hitter swung at.

## Hitting

**Chase rate**: Swings at pitches outside the strike zone ÷ pitches outside the zone. Bunt attempts are excluded.

**Zone swing / zone contact**: Swing rate on pitches in the zone, and contact rate on those swings.

**Whiff rate**: Swinging strikes ÷ swings. Foul tips count as whiffs, matching Baseball Savant.

**Hard-hit rate**: Share of balls in play hit 95+ mph.

**EV90**: The 90th-percentile exit velocity on balls in play. A steadier read on raw power than average or max exit velocity.

**xwOBA**: Expected weighted on-base average. Uses the expected value of each ball in play from exit velocity and launch angle, plus actual strikeouts, walks, and hit-by-pitches.

## Conventions

**Percentiles** rank a player against the qualified league pool (150+ PA or batters faced) and are **oriented so higher is always better**, so a low chase rate or a low walk rate allowed shows as a high percentile. Unqualified players are placed against the same qualified pool.

**Δ14** compares the final (or most recent) 14 days with the season to date. Rates are in percentage points. [Why two weeks is enough for some numbers and not others](/baseball/two-week-signal/).

**Strike zone** means Statcast zones 1–9.
